newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bank Austria not best fit for CA - Bacob.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria not best fit for CA - Bacob.

text.p: Bank Austria is not the best candidate to buy the Austrian state's 70 percent voting stake in flagship bank Creditanstalt, the Belgian member of a rival bidding consortium said on Friday.

A spokesman for Belgian Bacob bank told Reuters that even if Bank Austria's bid price for Creditanstalt were higher, the rival consortium led by insurer EA-Generali to which Bacob belongs is a more logical partner for Creditanstalt.

"If the biggest Asutrian bank (Bank Austria) buys the second-biggest (Creditanstalt), the rationalisation proces will lead to job losses, which the government should also factor in," Bacob spokesman Guido Mertens told Reuters.
Secondly, a Bank Austria-CA merger would raise anti-trust issues for the Austrian banking industry, as the new bank would become six times bigger than its closest competitor, he said.
He also said that as Bank Austria is majority owned by the Austrian state and the city of Vienna, a sale to Bank Austria would not really be a privatisation.
"Our offer, however, could lead to a lot of synergies, notably in banking-insurance," he said.
He declined to say how big Bacob's part of the EA- Generali consortium is.
Bank Austria has offered 16.8 billion schillings for Creditanstalt and said today it had improved its bid. EA-Generali has offered 13.8 billion and has also said it has bettered its bid.
The Austrian government is due to announce its choice before Tuesday. -- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
